newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu endorses arch-foe as Zaire premier.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu endorses arch-foe as Zaire premier.

text.p: President Mobutu Sese Seko on Wednesday approved the appointment of his arch-rival and opposition firebrand Etienne Tshisekedi as Zaire's new prime minister, state radio announced.
"The president of the republic ratifies and names Tshisekedi wa Mulumba as Prime Minister and head of the transitional government," the radio said.
Mobutu's spokesman Kabuya Lumuna confirmed the radio report.
"The decree has been signed," Kabuya told Reuters.
He said a meeting between the two men was arranged earlier on Wednesday evening, but he could not confirm whether it had taken place.
Constitutionally Mobutu was simply charged with signing an endorsement of a candidate chosen by parliament.
Lawmakers on Tuesday nominated Tshisekedi, a former prime minister, to head the government and steer Zaire through negotiations with rebels who hold a quarter of the vast Central African country.
Tshisekedi has long favoured talks with rebel chief Laurent Kabila to end the war launched from eastern Zaire in October.
But the rebels are pressing on with their military campaign in which they have put the demoralised Zaire army on the run, and many Zaireans believe Tshisekedi will be Mobutu's last prime minister.
